title: iriguchi.errors/1-draft
description: Every named failure iriguchi can print, the exceptions it raises and never prints, and one sentence each in two languages. **This is not an error.** It is a catalogue, the same on every run, and a consumer reads it once at build time so that a failure arriving at three in the morning already has a name it knows.

by.description: Producer, as name/version. A kind added in a later version is absent here, which is the staleness a consumer's build is testing for.

errors.description:
**The closed set.** Every kind iriguchi prints as the name before the colon on the first line of stderr when it exits non-zero.

`[]` is a valid answer and means *this build has no named failures*. It is not the same as the field being absent, which would mean nobody had asked the question.

open_namespaces.description:
Prefixes whose second half comes from a foreign vocabulary iriguchi cannot enumerate -- the arrangement `iriguchi.rules/1-draft` uses for `presidio.` and `mamori.`.

iriguchi's is empty, and that is a claim rather than an omission: every kind above is one of its own class names, because an adapter that catches a foreign exception wraps it before it can reach the top-level handler.

not_a_failure.description:
**The half a catalogue of errors normally cannot say.** These are raised, and a person never sees them as failures: ADR-0002 turns a broken proposer into the most restrictive route available with a reason naming what broke, so it arrives as a *decision*.

Without this field a consumer reading `errors` would conclude that a broken scanner produces nothing. It produces a routing decision, and `reported_as` says which rule identifier carries it.

kind.description: The stable identifier, spelled exactly as it appears before the colon on the first line of stderr. This is the fold key: a consumer collapsing repeated failures into one row groups on this and keeps nothing else, because the sentence after the colon can quote what was handed in.

exit_code.description:
The process exit code that always accompanies this kind.

iriguchi's codes are `0` decided, `2` refused, `1` broken -- and **`2` is a decision, not a failure**, which is why no entry here carries it. A refusal has a routing decision on standard output and belongs to `iriguchi.routing-decision/1`.

outcome.description: What happened, in the consumer's vocabulary. Narrower than the exit code: `1` is every named failure here, and these four are what a screen needs to distinguish.

retryable.description:
**Not a forecast.** Whether the same request may be issued again, unchanged -- a question about permission, not about possibility. A failure where re-issuing is itself a new event (it leaves the machine, it is billed, it leaves a trace) is `false` even when it could succeed.

Every entry in this build is `false`, which is a statement rather than an oversight. `ModelError` is the one that is not obvious: on the outbound path it is raised after the send has already happened, so re-issuing sends the prompt a second time. One kind spans the local path and the outbound one, and the answer for a kind that spans them is the restrictive one. Recovering local retry would mean splitting the kind, which is a change to the exception tree rather than to this document.

detail.description: One sentence about **what the kind means**, in English. Not what happened on a particular run -- the sentence after the colon on stderr says that, and it is the half a consumer is asked not to keep.

detail_ja.description: The same sentence in Japanese, **authored rather than translated**, for the reason `iriguchi.rules/1-draft` gives: iriguchi owns the meaning of its own failures, so both sentences are written by the same hand and cannot disagree.

error.$comment: No message template, and no example of a real path. Both were asked for to be left out, and the reason is that a reader fills a template in from their own logs -- at which point a document that holds no values is a document that holds values.

reported_as.description: The rule identifier that carries it into a decision instead. Resolvable in `iriguchi.rules/1-draft`, and a test drives it through that document -- the first draft of this catalogue pointed at `routing.judge-failed`, which does not exist.

$comment:
A draft. It freezes when a second program both produces and consumes it, which is the family's rule -- and the rule is about a program that used it and found something, not about a validator that accepted it. Sora is the consumer; no second producer exists yet.

Three invariants JSON Schema cannot express, all enforced by `tests/test_the_error_catalogue_is_complete.py`:

**`errors` is complete.** Every `IriguchiError` subclass is in `errors`, in `not_a_failure`, or declared in `errors.NOT_YET_RAISED` as raised by nothing.

**`exit_code` is driven, for every kind.** Each declared code is the code the top-level handler actually returns when that kind is raised, and the name it prints first -- measured by raising each one at a seam inside the handler rather than by reading the table. `ConfigurationError` is additionally driven through a real failing command. This is a claim about the handler, not about reachability: whether a kind can arise at all is what `errors.NOT_YET_RAISED` answers, and a kind declared there is refused a place in `errors`.

**The two lists never overlap**, and `reported_as` resolves in the rules catalogue.
